What happened?

The timeline of 16 November 2026, from Lighter's public data.

TraderSwift case study1 min readRead Markdown ↗

All times are UTC on 16 November. The pool and withdrawal times come from Lighter's public account data and the Ethereum chain.

TimeEvent
09:40A zero-fee public pool is created under the victim's account
10:1110,393,056.79 USDC is paid out of Lighter's L1 contract to the attacker (Cointelegraph)
10:25A second zero-fee pool is created under a second account
11:02Lighter suspends all withdrawals and pool creation (Lighter)
12:49Lighter: the incident "was caused by a leaked API key for a specific trader's account. The Lighter protocol and smart contracts are unaffected." (Lighter)

Lighter's public account data showed two withdrawals requested to the attacker: 10,393,056.79 and 5,096,588.02 USDC, about $15.5 million (crypto.news).

The first was paid out on Ethereum. The second was held. Lighter said its priority was to recover the funds in that "additional withdrawal attempt", and its Security Council later returned about $5 million to the trader (Lighter, Crypto Briefing).

Lighter has not confirmed a total.
